reading.title: Bioluminescence in Deep-Sea Organisms
reading.passage: Bioluminescence is the production of light by living organisms through chemical reactions. In deep-sea environments where sunlight cannot penetrate, many creatures have evolved this remarkable ability. Fish, squid, and jellyfish use bioluminescence for various purposes including attracting prey, communicating with potential mates, and confusing predators. Scientists estimate that nearly 90% of deep-sea organisms produce light. This adaptation represents millions of years of evolution in one of Earth's most extreme habitats, enabling survival in complete darkness.

questions.q: According to the passage, what is the primary purpose of bioluminescence in deep-sea organisms?
options: To warm their bodies in cold water
To attract prey, communicate, and confuse predators
questions.explanation: 지문에서 '어류, 오징어, 해파리는 생물발광을 먹이를 끌어당기고, 짝짓기 대상과 소통하고, 포식자를 혼동하기 위해 사용한다'고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.q: Why do deep-sea organisms need bioluminescence?
options: Because sunlight penetrates deep into the ocean
Because sunlight cannot penetrate deep-sea environments
Because it helps them move faster
questions.explanation: 지문의 첫 번째 문장 이후에 '햇빛이 도달할 수 없는 깊은 바다 환경에서 많은 생물들이 이 놀라운 능력을 진화시켰다'고 설명하고 있습니다.

questions.q: What does the passage suggest about the prevalence of bioluminescence?
options: It is rare among deep-sea creatures
Nearly 90% of deep-sea organisms produce light
questions.explanation: 지문에서 '과학자들은 거의 90%의 심해 생물이 빛을 생산한다고 추정한다'고 직접 언급하고 있습니다.

writing.prompt: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement: Technology has improved human relationships rather than damaged them? Use specific reasons and examples to support your answer.

structure.intro: 명확한 입장 표현 (동의 또는 불동의)과 2-3개의 핵심 이유 미리 제시. 예: 'Technology has significantly improved human relationships because it enables long-distance communication, allows us to maintain connections, and helps people with common interests find each other.'
structure.body1: 첫 번째 이유와 구체적 예시 제시. 예를 들어, 원거리 가족 간 비디오 통화의 중요성을 설명.
structure.body2: 두 번째 이유로 상반된 관점 인정하면서도 강화. 예: 소셜 미디어의 부정적 측면을 언급하되, 어떻게 긍정적 측면이 더 크다고 주장할 것인지 설명.
structure.conclusion: 입장 재확인 및 사회적 함의 언급. 기술 자체가 아닌 사용 방식이 중요함을 제시.

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer to work in a large company with many employees. Others prefer to work in a small company or start their own business. Which do you prefer and why?
useful_expressions: In my opinion, I prefer working in a small company because
One reason is that small companies offer more opportunities for
Another advantage is that employees in small organizations can
This is important to me because
sample_points: 소규모 회사에서는 개인의 기여가 더 눈에 띄고 인정받으며, 더 빠른 승진과 성장 기회가 있습니다. 예시: 자신의 아이디어가 직접 경영진에게 전달되고 빠르게 실행될 수 있습니다.
대규모 회사의 안정성은 좋지만 창의성과 자율성이 제한될 수 있습니다. 소규모 회사에서는 다양한 부서 일을 경험하며 폭넓은 기술을 배울 수 있습니다.

listening.title: Campus Library Discussion
listening.script: Student: Hi, I'm looking for information about the new study rooms in the library. Librarian: Oh yes, we just opened them last week. They're designed for group projects and have whiteboards, computers, and comfortable seating. Student: That sounds great! How do I reserve one? Librarian: You can reserve them online through the library website or come to the front desk. Each room can be booked for up to three hours. Student: Perfect! Are there any restrictions? Librarian: Yes, you need to be quiet and keep the rooms clean. Also, food and drinks are allowed except for beverages that might spill easily. We want to maintain a professional study environment. Student: Got it. This is really helpful. I think my study group will love these new facilities. Librarian: Great! Feel free to ask if you have any other questions.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the new study rooms?
options: To provide a place for individual quiet study
To allow students to eat meals together
To serve as group project spaces with technology
To replace the existing library computers
questions.explanation: 도서관 사서가 '그룹 프로젝트를 위해 설계되었으며 화이트보드, 컴퓨터, 편안한 좌석이 있다'고 명확히 설명했습니다.

questions.q: How long can each room be reserved for at a time?
questions.explanation: 사서가 '각 방은 최대 3시간까지 예약할 수 있다'고 직접 언급했습니다.

questions.q: What type of drinks are NOT allowed in the study rooms?
questions.explanation: 사서가 '음료 중에서 쏟아질 수 있는 음료는 허용되지 않는다'고 구체적으로 설명했습니다.
